Regular Meeting Notice
                   Truckee-Donner Recreation and Park District Board of Directors
                              Thursday, October 22, 2026, 4:00 P.M.
                  Steve Randall Community Recreation Center, 10981 Truckee Way

The Board of Directors welcomes you to its meeting. Your interest is encouraged and appreciated.
Copies of the agenda and correspondence may be obtained at the District office.

1. OPEN MEETING

2. ROLL CALL

matter not on the agenda. Please state your name for the record. Comments are limited to three minutes
in order for all interested parties to have an opportunity to speak. No action shall be taken by the board
on items not appearing on the agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2 – Brown Act). The board may
choose to acknowledge the comment or, where appropriate, briefly answer a question, refer the matter to
staff, or set the item for discussion at a future meeting.

     1. Item is presented by staff or applicant.

     3. Public comment – Limited to three minutes.

Truckee-Donner Recreation and Park District
                        Policy Handbook


POLICY TITLE:                Boundaries for Employees and Volunteers Interacting
                             with Minors

POLICY NUMBER:               247


247.10       This policy applies to all permanent full-time employees, part-time
benefited employees, seasonal/part-time employees, and volunteers who work directly
with minors. A minor is defined as a person who is under the legal age of an adult, or
anyone under the age of 18 years of age.

247.20        Boundaries are defined to guide Recreation and Park staff in conducting
themselves in a way that reflects the high standards of behavior and professionalism
required of employees and volunteers and to specify boundaries between minors and
staff. The term “Boundaries” is defined as acceptable professional behavior by
employees and volunteers while interacting with minors. Trespassing beyond the
Boundaries of a minor and employee/volunteer relationship is deemed an abuse of
power and a betrayal of public trust.

247.30         This policy attempts to clearly define the boundaries, so everyone
understands the expectations and the consequences of not obeying them. Staff shall
respect the individual rights of minors and act in their best interest. Minors shall not be
discriminated against regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation,
religion, socioeconomic status, or disability. The District shall have zero tolerance for
harassment or abuse.

247.40        Some activities may seem innocent from an employee’s perspective, but
some of these can be perceived as flirtation or sexual insinuation from a minor or
parental point of view. The purpose of the following lists of acceptable and
unacceptable behaviors is not to restrain innocent, positive relationships between
employees and minors but to prevent relationships that could lead to, or may be
perceived as, misconduct.

247.50        The following is an illustrative list of unacceptable behavior, which
includes but is not limited to:

   •   Remarks about the physical attributes or physiological development of anyone.
   •   Excessive attention toward a particular minor.
   •   Sending e-mails, text messages, instant messages, social media messages, or
       letters to minors if the content is not about park and recreation activities and not
       in accordance with applicable District policies or in violation of the District’s
       Social Media and/or Technology Policy.

                                 T-D.R.P.D. POLICY HANDBOOK
          Policy #247 - “Boundaries for Employees and Volunteers Interacting with Minors”
                                    Approved October 22, 2026

Item #: 6.4 - Resolution #2026-363 Designating District Agents for the FFY 2024 State
and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program

Presenter: Brian Compton, IT Administrator

Recommendation:
     Approve Resolution #2026-363 designating the General Manager, Accounting
     Manager, and IT Administrator as Authorized Agents of the District for the
     Federal Fiscal Year 2024 State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program and
     authorizing those agents to execute and submit the documents required by the
     Cal OES.

Background:
     In March 2026, the Truckee-Donner Recreation and Park District submitted a
     proposal to the California Governor's Office of Emergency Services for funding
     through the Federal Fiscal Year 2024 State and Local Cybersecurity Grant
     Program. The District's proposal was subsequently selected for funding.

       The proposed Secure Cloud Transition and Cyber Resilience Program is
       intended to improve the District's cybersecurity governance, identity and device
       management, cloud security, threat detection and response, data protection,
       recovery capabilities, network security, and employee cybersecurity awareness.
       The project supports the District's transition from legacy on-premises technology
       to modern cloud services and related cybersecurity controls.

       The District requested $249,941.33 in federal funding. The proposed project
       includes a required 30% local match of $107,117.71, resulting in a total
       estimated project cost of $357,059.04. The anticipated project period is July 1,
       2026 through August 31, 2028.

       As part of the post-award process, Cal OES requires the District to adopt a
       Governing Body Resolution identifying the positions authorized to act on behalf
       of the District. Cal OES recommends identifying more than one Authorized
       Agent, and all required grant documents must be signed by an Authorized Agent
       whose position matches the Governing Body Resolution.



   10981 Truckee Way, Truckee, CA 96161 | Phone: (530) 582-7720 | Fax: (530) 582-7724 | www.tdrpd.org
